receipt.public_excerpt: performance gains from bigger models have plateaued.

evidence_items.explanation: This contemporary report identifies Sutskever and explicitly describes his acknowledgment of a plateau. It is reputable secondary reporting of his position; the underlying Reuters interview was inaccessible through read_page.

evidence_items.publisher: The New York Times, syndicated by The Indian Express
evidence_items.locator: Hassabis interview passage following the discussion of scaling laws and available text

receipt.public_excerpt: no longer getting the same progress.

evidence_items.explanation: The report attributes this statement to Google DeepMind leader Demis Hassabis and explicitly describes his view that returns from adding training data were diminishing. It also preserves his qualification that existing techniques could still deliver improvements.

evidence_items.locator: Interview answer beginning 'To be very clear about my answer'

receipt.public_excerpt: it’s not just a question of scaling alone

evidence_items.explanation: In an original interview conducted Wednesday before publication, Google CEO Sundar Pichai explains that further progress requires breakthroughs beyond scaling alone. This supports the qualified reading of Marcus's sentence, although Pichai remained optimistic and did not declare that AI progress had stopped.

evidence_items.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Indeed, we may already', in the discussion of scaling laws

receipt.public_excerpt: perhaps already approaching a point of diminishing returns.

evidence_items.explanation: The dated article directly establishes that Marcus voiced a similar warning in 2022, in a discussion that includes GPT-3-like models. It is used only as a record of his statement, not as evidence that his technical assessment was right.

evidence_items.publisher: The New York Times, syndicated by The Indian Express
evidence_items.locator: Paragraph introducing the positions of Altman, Amodei and Huang
evidence_items.explanation: The report also identifies Sam Altman, Dario Amodei and Jensen Huang as optimistic about continued progress. This limits any reading of Marcus's statement as an industry consensus, but does not negate the existence of the cited acknowledgments.

unresolved_gaps: Marcus gives no count for 'many'; the selected records establish three prominent figures, two at the same company.
Pichai's statement acknowledges the need for breakthroughs more clearly than it acknowledges an already-observed decline in marginal returns.
The records establish public positions, not the actual technical performance of every major laboratory's scaling efforts.
